$comment: Shared VfStepper cases. Plain data only: no Vue, no PHP, no renderer objects. Each adapter maps these neutral fields onto its own API. The vocabulary is the historical Vue contract at fd793696f50d3be0fcd3788f0f8f751c63869963. The second catalog for a component that owns controls, and the first where one instance owns several of the same role: every case declares `componentInteractive`, the number of triggers the component renders - one per item, across every instance in the case, zero for an empty list - and `consumerInteractive` only when a consumer control stands beside the stepper (it has no slots). An interaction case names the gesture, the semantic effect it must produce on every target - aria-current, item classes, the trigger's own modifier, the progress factor, focus, prevented keys and the event log as separate claims - and the initial case whose DOM the result must converge on. scripts/ci/stepper-coverage.mjs is what stops the list eroding.

propVocabulary.items: VfStepperItem[], required. Each item is { value, label, description?, disabled? }. Rendered in order as li.vf-stepper__item > button.vf-stepper__trigger; the description span exists only for a non-empty description; disabled writes the native attribute on the trigger.
propVocabulary.modelValue: string | undefined, default undefined. The controlled value; wins whenever defined, an empty string included. A Vue consumer pairs it with update:modelValue (v-model). The Razor adapter reads it as the initial value and selects on its own.
propVocabulary.defaultValue: string | undefined. Seeds the uncontrolled state once; an unknown or disabled value is kept as-is.
propVocabulary.orientation: 'horizontal' | 'vertical', default horizontal. Decides the modifier class and which arrow keys navigate.
propVocabulary.contentPosition: 'above' | 'below' (horizontal) or 'start' | 'end' (vertical). A position from the other axis resolves to that axis's default.
propVocabulary.ariaLabel: string, default 'Progress'. The nav's accessible name.

contentVocabulary.beside: A consumer control rendered as a sibling *after* the stepper's root, inside the case: `control` is a real consumer button. The stepper renders no slot; this is the only way a consumer control can share a case with it.

groupVocabulary: A list of sibling steppers rendered side by side in one case, each with its own props; the case-level props are ignored. Values must be distinct between members: the reference moves keyboard focus with a document-wide lookup, and a shared value would make a keyboard case depend on document order.

ownershipVocabulary.componentInteractive: The exact number of controls the component itself renders in this case: one button.vf-stepper__trigger per item, summed over every instance. Zero for an empty list. Asserted on every target against the measured component-owned controls, and their tag identity against the profile - a div with role=button is not a trigger, and a disabled trigger is still the component's.
ownershipVocabulary.consumerInteractive: The exact number of consumer controls in the case. Zero unless a `beside` control is declared.

interactionVocabulary.$comment: A case with an `interaction` is driven in the browser with real pointer and key events, then re-measured: the snapshot, the DOM and the accessibility tree are all taken again.
interactionVocabulary.steps: clickButton (a real pointer click at the trigger's centre; `index` picks a trigger in document order across every instance), focusButton (`index` likewise), pressKey with Enter, Space, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home or End.
interactionVocabulary.expect: Claims checked against the snapshot on every target. `activates` is whether a native click reached a trigger - true for a pointer click and for Enter/Space, which the reference leaves to native activation, false for every handled navigation key. `currentValue` is the value of the trigger carrying aria-current in the first instance (null when none), `currentValues` the same per instance, `currentClassValue` the value of the trigger carrying vf-stepper__trigger--current - claimed separately so a port that moved one and not the other fails. `itemStates` is the item modifier of every item in order, `progressFactor` the inline --vf-stepper-progress-factor of the first root, `disabledValues` the triggers with the native attribute. `focusValue` is the value of the focused trigger (null when focus is elsewhere) and `focusRole` where focus is when it is not on a trigger. `keydownPrevented` is whether each keydown of the scenario was prevented, in order: a handled navigation key is, Enter, Space and a wrong-axis arrow are not. `events` is the neutral change log the fixture keeps: one entry per change notification with its value. A key of the form `a11y:<role>.<state>` is a claim about the accessibility tree read after the action.
interactionVocabulary.matches: The initial case whose DOM the post-interaction DOM must equal on the same target. Every stepper item persists across a selection change, so the result of a gesture has to be exactly the DOM a fresh render of the target state produces.
interactionVocabulary.notClaimable: `a11y:<trigger>.current`: Chrome 153 exposes no changing `current` property for button[aria-current=step] through the CDP accessibility tree, so the current step is proved by the live DOM (currentValue, itemStates) and never by the tree. See the policy.

cases.title: Nothing given: the first enabled item is current, the rest upcoming, factor 0
cases.$why: The fallback itself. A port that seeded nothing would render no current step; one that seeded the first item regardless of disabled is told apart by stepper/disabled-first.

cases.title: defaultValue seeds the middle step: one complete, one current, one upcoming, factor 0.5
defaultValue seeds the last step: everything before it complete, factor 1
The controlled modelValue alone
The controlled modelValue on the last step
modelValue wins over defaultValue
cases.$why: The precedence measured in the one direction where the two props disagree. A port that read defaultValue first would mark the middle step current.

cases.title: An unknown modelValue: no step current, every enabled step upcoming, factor normalised to 0
cases.$why: The reference keeps the value and matches nothing; it does not fall back. A port that 'fixed' this to the first step would carry aria-current somewhere.

cases.title: An empty-string modelValue is a value, not an absence: no step current
cases.$why: The ?? boundary. A port testing truthiness would fall through to the fallback and mark the first step current.

cases.title: A disabled middle step: native disabled on its trigger, the disabled modifier on its item, and nothing else
A disabled middle step with the last step current: complete, disabled, current
cases.$why: Disabled beats complete: the middle step is before the active one and is still reported disabled, not complete.

cases.title: The first step disabled: the fallback is the second step, factor 0.5
cases.$why: The fallback is the first *enabled* item. A port seeding items[0] would mark a disabled step current.

cases.title: The first step disabled with the last step current: disabled, complete, current
The last step disabled with the first current: current, upcoming, disabled
The last step disabled with the middle current: complete, current, disabled
defaultValue names a disabled step: it is the active value, so the step before it is complete, but nothing carries aria-current
cases.$why: The watch is not immediate, so the disabled seed survives mount. State precedence puts disabled before current: complete, disabled, upcoming, factor 0.5, no aria-current anywhere.

cases.title: Every step disabled: no fallback, no current step, factor 0
No items: an empty list, the count custom property only
cases.$why: Zero component-owned controls is a legitimate budget for this component, and the root writes no factor for fewer than two items. Not screenshotted: an empty list paints nothing and has no height to clip; the DOM, style and ownership comparisons carry the case.

cases.title: One item: current, and the count only - no factor
Two items with the second current: factor 1
Four items with the second current: factor 1/3, written as JavaScript writes it
cases.$why: 0.3333333333333333 - sixteen digits. A server writing PHP's default fourteen would move the vertical rail by nothing a screenshot can see, and the style comparison would report it.

cases.title: Four items with the third current: factor 2/3
Seven items with the second current: factor 1/6, seventeen digits
Seven items with the sixth current: factor 5/6, the last digit rounded up
Vertical orientation: content-end by default
Vertical with the middle step current
Vertical with the content before the rail
A horizontal position on a vertical stepper resolves to the default: content-end
cases.$why: The other axis's position is the default, not an error. A port validating the union would throw or write content-above.

cases.title: Horizontal with the content above the rail
A vertical position on a horizontal stepper resolves to the default: content-below
Every step carries a description
No step carries a description: the description span is absent everywhere
Vertical with descriptions on every step
Labels and descriptions long enough to wrap

cases.title: A custom accessible name on the nav
A consumer class after the canonical ones and a consumer style after the root custom properties
Consumer id, data attribute, role and aria-current land on the nav, never on a trigger
cases.$why: inheritAttrs is false and everything but class is spread onto the nav. A consumer aria-current on the root must not disturb the trigger's own.

cases.title: Two steppers side by side with distinct values: each owns its own triggers and its own current step
cases.$why: Five component-owned controls across two instances. The values are deliberately distinct: the reference moves keyboard focus with a document-wide lookup, and a shared value would make the case order-dependent (see the policy's outsideTheCatalog).

cases.title: A consumer's own Continue button beside the stepper is the consumer's, not the component's
cases.$why: The one case with a non-zero consumer budget. The stepper has no slots, so a consumer control can only stand beside it; ownership must classify it by identity and leave the component's count at three.

cases.title: A real pointer click on the middle trigger moves the selection forward: aria-current, item classes, trigger class and factor all move, one change event
A click on the first trigger moves the selection backward
A click on the current trigger changes nothing and emits nothing
cases.$why: The native click reaches the trigger (activates) and the component suppresses the change: same state, empty log.

cases.title: A click on the middle trigger and then ArrowRight from it: navigation starts from the newly focused trigger
cases.$why: Two selection changes on a persistent DOM: the same three items carry three successive state layouts, and the log has both values in order.

cases.title: Enter on the focused middle trigger activates it natively: one click is counted, the selection moves
cases.$why: Section 20: the opposite of the accordion. There is no keydown handler for Enter; the browser synthesises the click. A port that handled Enter itself and prevented the default would record zero activations while the DOM moved.

cases.title: Space on the focused middle trigger activates it natively as well
Enter on the focused current trigger: the native click is counted and the component suppresses the change
ArrowRight from the first trigger of a horizontal stepper: prevented, the next step activated and focused, no native click
ArrowLeft from the last trigger goes to the previous step
ArrowDown on a horizontal stepper is ignored: not prevented, nothing moves, nothing is emitted
cases.$why: Section 21: the wrong axis is ignored *and* not prevented. A port that mapped both axes would move; one that prevented and ignored would trap the page's own scrolling.

cases.title: ArrowDown from the first trigger of a vertical stepper activates and focuses the next
ArrowUp from the middle trigger of a vertical stepper goes to the previous
ArrowRight on a vertical stepper is ignored and not prevented
Home from the last trigger activates and focuses the first enabled step
End from the first trigger activates and focuses the last enabled step
Home from the first trigger when it is already current: prevented, focus stays, nothing emitted
cases.$why: Activation is suppressed on the current step while the key is still handled: prevented, focus moved to the same trigger.

cases.title: ArrowRight from the first trigger skips the disabled middle step
ArrowLeft from the last trigger skips the disabled middle step
ArrowRight from the last trigger wraps to the first
ArrowLeft from the first trigger wraps to the last
Home with the first step disabled lands on the second
End with the last step disabled lands on the second
A disabled trigger takes no focus, so ArrowRight reaches nothing
cases.$why: A disabled button cannot take focus, so the key is pressed with focus on the body: it never reaches a trigger, no keydown is recorded in the case, and nothing moves.

cases.title: A v-model consumer: the click emits, the consumer writes the value back, the selection moves
cases.$why: The controlled protocol round-tripped through a consumer that accepts. The Razor adapter has no parent to ask and selects directly; all three land on the same state.

cases.title: Focusing the middle trigger changes nothing
Clicking a trigger in the second of two steppers moves its selection and leaves the first alone
cases.$why: State isolation between instances, measured per instance. Focus isolation is a separate claim the reference does not make (see the policy).

cases.title: ArrowUp in the vertical second stepper moves its selection and focus, and the first stepper is untouched
cases.$why: Keyboard navigation inside the second instance with distinct values: the focus lands in the second instance on every target, because no value is shared with the first.
